### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 115a43ad162cfe5ec96d2f7fe938afcae4290cf5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c628fd23cd31b300e9bf1efb5f326e37c60166dd` — the merge of head `dd7ed18f7456bbcb3b08139245e919ad6bc7875f` into base `115a43ad162cfe5ec96d2f7fe938afcae4290cf5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c628fd23cd31b300e9bf1efb5f326e37c60166dd && git checkout c628fd23cd31b300e9bf1efb5f326e37c60166dd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 115a43ad162cfe5ec96d2f7fe938afcae4290cf5 dd7ed18f7456bbcb3b08139245e919ad6bc7875f && git checkout -B drift-repro 115a43ad162cfe5ec96d2f7fe938afcae4290cf5 && git merge --no-ff dd7ed18f7456bbcb3b08139245e919ad6bc7875f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 115a43ad162cfe5ec96d2f7fe938afcae4290cf5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `da4e41dd206141a3a3a0b568e1df03d5239e5cd3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/marketplace/taxonomy.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/refinement-projection.ts + packages/spec/scripts/lib/refinement-projection.ts (the emit the arm's declaration claims), packages/spec/scripts/refinement-projection.test.ts (the pin the exactness argument cites), packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json (the rows the arm retires), packages/spec/src/marketplace/package.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/marketplace/marketplace.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/marketplace/template-manifest.zod.ts (the consumers that reach the 14 sites), packages/spec/src/shared/lazy-schema.ts (the Proxy the predicate identity survives), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/review-checklist.md (read for ②). Inputs: card #31036 body + its 3 comments (triage 6694081664, claim 6694406443, os-dev-report 6695323960), PR #31047 body, file list (6 files), net diff `origin/main` `9d939c58`...`da4e41dd`, the head's check-runs, and the live tree at `origin/main`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Runtime accept set — unchanged (right).** On `main`, `distinct()` refines with the inline arrow `(values) => new Set(values).size === values.length`; on the head it refines with `UNIQUE_SCALAR_ITEMS`, whose body is the identical expression `new Set(values).size === values.length` over the same array. `declare()` only registers the function in a module-private `WeakMap` and freezes the declaration object; it does not wrap, bind or alter the predicate. The chain is byte-identical otherwise: same `.refine(fn, { message })` with the same key-bearing message, same `.min(1)` / `.max(MAX_*)` / `.describe()` on both callers, no `abort`, no `path`. The only runtime-observable difference is the function's identity, which nothing but the projection reads. Same inputs pass and fail: `['sales']`, `['sales','marketing']` pass; `['sales','sales']`, `['sales','marketing','sales']` fail with `custom` + the helper's message; `[]` still fails `businessFunctions` on `min(1)` and passes `industries`; `['not-a-function']` still fails at the item. The head's "Zod parse is unchanged" case pins exactly this corpus and the issue tuple.
2. **The `T extends z.ZodType<JsonScalar>` bound — type-only (right).** Generic bounds erase; no emitted JS moves. Both live callers pass a `z.enum` of string literals, which satisfies the bound (zod 4's `ZodType` is covariant in its output parameter). Gate verdict: see ④/gates below for `Type Check · workspace`.
3. **Published JSON Schema — narrows at exactly 14 sites, all intended (right).** Read from the live tree, not the PR body: `distinct()` is file-local with exactly two callers, `MarketplaceBusinessFunctionsSchema` and `MarketplaceIndustriesSchema` (taxonomy.zod.ts:169, :182 on `main`). Every published schema that reaches them: the two facets themselves (root site `""`); `marketplace/Package` (package.zod.ts:255 `businessFunctions`, :258 `industries`); `marketplace/CreatePackageRequest` (:347, :348); `marketplace/UpdatePackageRequest` (:374, :375); `marketplace/MarketplaceListing` (marketplace.zod.ts:256, :259); `marketplace/TemplateManifest` (template-manifest.zod.ts:55-56 — derived from `CreatePackageRequestSchema` by `.omit()` / `.extend()`, which omits neither facet, so it inherits both properties); `marketplace/MarketplaceSearchResponse` (marketplace.zod.ts:483, `items: z.array(MarketplaceListingSchema)`, hence `items.element.businessFunctions` / `items.element.industries`). 2 + 2×6 = **14 sites in 8 schemas**, and these are exactly the 8 entries / 14 sites the ledger on `main` held for the facets (baseline.json:1277-1322) and the diff deletes. The `.optional()` wrappers at the six embedding sites do not move the check: the `custom` check sits on the `ZodArray` node and `.optional()` wraps outside it, so the override fires on the array node and the keyword lands on the property — the head's `Package` case asserts both properties.
4. **Nothing else gains `uniqueItems` (right).** `UNIQUE_SCALAR_ITEMS` is composed nowhere on the head but `distinct()`. The other two `Set`-uniqueness refinements in `packages/spec/src` keep their unregistered inline arrows and therefore stay `dropped`: `security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts:79` (`organizationIds`) and `data/object.zod.ts:3416` (`groups` unique by `key` — uniqueness of a projection, not of items, and correctly not this arm). `emitUniqueItems` writes only on a node whose `custom` check's `fn` is the registered function, so no array without the declared predicate is touched; the generator leaves every other node byte for byte as zod emitted it. Zod never emits `uniqueItems` itself, so no pre-existing keyword can be overwritten.
5. **`uniqueItems` is exact on the scalar types the live enums allow (right), and on JSON scalars generally (right, with one documentation gap — ④ should-fix).** The 14 sites' items are string-literal enums. JSON Schema 2020-12 §4.2.2 equality on strings is "same code points", which coincides with SameValueZero on JS strings (same code-unit sequence), so `Set` and `uniqueItems` are one relation on every list these sites can carry; `'Sales'` vs `'sales'` are two to both. For the arm's full `JsonScalar` domain: `0` / `-0` — `Set` (SameValueZero) says one, JSON Schema (mathematical value) says one; `JSON.parse('[0,-0]')` does yield `-0` and the head's test asserts both sides refuse it. `NaN` and `±Infinity` are not JSON and `z.number()` refuses non-finite values, so neither reaches the predicate from a document. `"1"` vs `1`, `true` vs `1`, `false` / `0` / `""` / `null` — different JSON types, two to both (`Set` keys on type as well). `1` vs `1.0` — one number after `JSON.parse`, one to both. `null` vs `null` — one to both. Exactness direction: on scalars a deterministic parse maps JSON-equal values to SameValueZero-equal values, so the predicate can never refuse a list the keyword accepts, and vice versa — the file neither over-narrows nor stays wider at these sites.
6. **The eight ledger rows retired (right).** Deletions only; no site added or moved elsewhere in the file. `measured.publishedSchemasWithDroppedRefinements` 260→252 and `droppedRefinementSites` 1037→1023 are the arithmetic of the 8 entries / 14 sites and are pinned against the entries by `scripts/dropped-refinements.test.ts:369-371`. `refinementSitesThatDidProject` 369→728 is NOT pinned by any gate (the dev says so, and the tree agrees: nothing in `build-schemas.ts` or the detector reads it); its correctness rests on the dev's build census (`728`, of which `14 unique-items`) — accepted as a hand-kept field with no reader, flagged in ③.
7. **Public surface.** `src/shared/refinement-projection.ts` gains two exports, `JsonScalar` and `UNIQUE_SCALAR_ITEMS`. The module is not on the package's `exports` map (`./shared` points elsewhere; the module is imported only by relative path from sibling `src/**` files), so these are not a published TypeScript surface — consistent with `check:generated` reporting the api-surface artifact unchanged. Not a Clause-② widening.
8. **Reference pages do not move (right).** The reference renderer (`scripts/lib/format-type.ts`) does not read `uniqueItems`, and `check:generated` reports 14/14 artifacts up to date; the docs-drift check on the PR derives no anchor from the ledger file, which is expected for a JSON ledger.

### ② Semver level

**Level: `patch` — right. Declaration: `Clause-②: no` with no arm — wrong; the arm `(narrowing)` is owed, and with it the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition marker. Must-fix.**

- The diff narrows a PUBLISHED accept set: `packages/spec/json-schema/**` ships in the tarball (`files[]` carries `json-schema`; `./openapi.json` is exported) and after this change refuses documents at 14 sites it accepted before. That the runtime already refused them is why the value is `no` (the question the value answers is 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」 — it does not widen), and it is exactly the case the arm exists for: `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs:90-99` — "A diff that NARROWS a published accept set answers it `no` truthfully — and a narrowing is a breaking change … `no (narrowing)` — NOT a widening, but breaking. This is the whole point of the arm." An ABSENT arm "declares NO DIRECTION" (clause2-line.mjs:104-108), which is the #16296 hole the arm was introduced to close: a narrowing shipped to consumers with every gate green. The seat's own claim (comment 6694406443) names the work "a narrowing of a published schema" while declaring `Clause-②: no` without the arm; the dev copied it and asked for a re-ruling in Acceptance notes. The ruling: **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`**.
- Precedent is unanimous on the arm. All five earlier arms of this same closed list shipped with the arm, a `**BREAKING (published artifact narrows)**` banner and an `<!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) … -->` marker (CHANGELOG.md: `dependentRequired` 72c1640, `banned-keys` 5eebc9e, `banned-key-pattern` 170fd83, all `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`), and the newer accept-set-declaration catch-up 81b4599 (`select` / `$select`, "the doors already refused it with a 400") shipped as `fix(spec)!` with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. `yes (narrowing)` on the five arms means "widens one surface and narrows another" under the current reader; nothing here widens, so `no (narrowing)` is the exact spelling, not `yes`.
- The LEVEL is right. Under maintainer ruling A (2026-10-21, #25105; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs:899-910`, AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3) the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone: `none` ⇒ `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct — the set of metadata documents an author can write is byte-for-byte what it was (the parse refused duplicates before and after). The sibling arm's `minor` (170fd83, 17.5.0) predates ruling A, when the `(narrowing)` arm was coupled to `minor` (no-major.mjs:901-904); it is not the rule now. So the changeset should read `'@objectstack/spec': patch` — as it does — and NOT `minor`.
- What the changeset and PR body must carry, concretely: (i) `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in both; (ii) a `**BREAKING (published artifact narrows)**` banner in the changeset body — the ADR-0087 gate reads the arm as a breaking signal (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:729`) and then asks for the disposition, so (iii) exactly one `<!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) … -->` marker in the changeset body, as every prior arm carried; (iv) the PR body's third line `Skills-docs: none — REASON` (a `(narrowing)` arm owes it, pm-dispatch SKILL.md:313; the reference renderer prints no `uniqueItems` and no skill teaches the facets' duplicate rule); (v) the dogfood battery pinned on the head before enqueue (`review-checklist.md:48`: `!` or `(narrowing)` ⇒ `dogfood_battery` on head, missing ⇒ REWORK) — the dev skipped it on the strength of the missing arm. The changeset's sentence "**Not a behaviour change.**" is true of the runtime and may stay beside the banner, as the prior arms' entries do.
- `Check Changeset` is green on the head because the current declaration is well-formed; it does not judge direction. The fix above keeps it green (`no (narrowing)` is a legal spelling for the one shared reader) and makes `check:adr-0087-registration` ask for the marker, which (iii) supplies.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Declared deviation 1 (Zod schema edit, seat ruling A 20:12Z/20:14Z) — answered, holds.** The claim's file surface excluded the Zod schemas; the projection keys on function identity (`DECLARED` WeakMap, `projectableRefinementOf(ruleOf(check))`) and refuses `fn.toString()` by design, so an inline arrow cannot be projected without the swap. The swap and the type-only bound are the three lines the ruling allowed and nothing else moved in the file; ①.1 and ①.2 judge them right.
- **Deviation 2 (`measured.refinementSitesThatDidProject` 369→728)** — answered: no gate reads it (①.6); accepted as the dev's census on this head. Not re-derived here (read-only). A later build that disagrees fails nothing, which is the pre-existing state of that field.
- **Deviation 3 (no assignee/reviewer on the PR)** — frame-level, not a contract matter; nothing to judge here.
- **Deviation 4 (`git checkout --detach` on the shared checkout; `git fetch --unshallow`)** — box hygiene, out of this record's faces.
- **Acceptance note "Clause-② reading … the seat can re-rule"** — answered in ②: re-ruled to `no (narrowing)`, level stays `patch`.
- **Acceptance note "Other `Set`-uniqueness refinements left alone"** — agreed and correct in both directions: `tenant-layer0-verdict.ts:79` is the same shape and could compose the predicate in a later card (it is outside this card's surface; the dev's `out_of_scope_findings` names it, carrier: none — the seat should file it so the ledger row has an owner); `object.zod.ts:3416` is not this arm.
- **`open_questions: []`** — none to answer.
- **Dogfood battery "n/a — no `!` and no `(narrowing)` arm"** — becomes owed once ② is applied; carried as part of the ② must-fix.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` relay for `os-tesla` (PR `user.login` per attribution comment); no non-fleet author to name.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/shared/refinement-projection.ts — holds; one should-fix.**

- *Against the module's own contract for a new arm* ("a factory or a pinned equivalence, an exact-equality argument in its own docblock, and the generator-side keywords that emit it"): all three present. The arm is the shared-constant shape, not a factory, for the same reason `NON_BLANK_STRING` is — nothing per call site to declare — and it is registered through the same `declare()` with a frozen `{ pattern: 'unique-items' }`, so `projectableRefinementOf` resolves it identically to the five existing arms; `PROJECTABLE_REFINEMENT_PATTERNS` gains the tag and the roster pin in the test is updated. The equivalence is pinned, not argued: the test evaluates `uniqueItems` with a deliberately non-`Set` JSON-equality evaluator over a corpus that includes the two scalar pairs where SameValueZero and JSON equality could diverge, asserts equality (not implication) in both directions, and refuses to pass vacuously when the keyword is absent. The `@ts-expect-error` compile-time pin is live: `tsconfig.scripts.json` includes `scripts/**/*`, and `Type Check · source gates` is green on the head.
- *Against the generator half (`scripts/lib/refinement-projection.ts`)*: `emitUniqueItems` writes `uniqueItems: true` beside the node's own keywords with no `allOf`. That is the right placement for this keyword and the reasoning is sound: `uniqueItems` is a boolean a validator reads on the array node, `true` is its only value here, zod never emits it, and it is not a keyword `format-type.ts` reads as a type (the `anyOf` hazard that forces `emitRequiredOneOf` to nest). Idempotent by construction. The `switch` is exhaustive over the union; the new `case` returns like its siblings.
- *Against the Proxy seam (`lazy-schema.ts`)*: both facets are `lazySchema` wrappers; the `_zod` facade prototype-delegates `def`, so `customChecksOf` reads the same check objects and the same `fn` through the Proxy — the mechanism every existing arm already relies on, and the head's census case reads all 8 schemas `projected` naming `unique-items`.
- *Trying to break it* — **should-fix (documentation + one guard in the docblock), not must-fix:** the exactness argument in the arm's docblock rests on item TYPE alone, but the predicate judges the parsed OUTPUT while `uniqueItems` judges the DOCUMENT. `z.ZodType<JsonScalar>` bounds the output type only, so an item schema whose parse is not the identity on scalars — `z.coerce.number()`, `z.coerce.string()`, `z.string().trim()`, `.toLowerCase()`, any `.transform()` to a scalar — satisfies the bound; on such an item `[1, "1"]` (coerce) or `['a', ' a']` (trim) is one value to the runtime and two to the keyword, so the published file would read `projected` while being WIDER than the runtime at that site — the ledger would then certify a gap. The direction is never the refusing one (a deterministic scalar map sends JSON-equal values to equal outputs), so no document the runtime accepts becomes refused, but "exact" would be false and the ledger silent. The two live callers are plain `z.enum` and are exact; the hazard is for the next composer. Fix: a ⛔ paragraph in the `unique-items` arm docblock and on `UNIQUE_SCALAR_ITEMS` stating the item schema must parse as the identity on scalars (`z.enum`, `z.literal`, `z.string()`, `z.number()`, `z.boolean()`, `z.null()`; ⛔ no coercion, trim, case-fold or transform), and ideally a line in `distinct()` saying the same. (Same note may record that for `z.number()` items two JSON numerals beyond 2^53 that round to one double are one to the predicate and two to a validator reading mathematical value — again the wider direction, unreachable at the live sites.)
- Nothing else found. `JsonScalar` is the right name and the right four-member union (JSON has no fifth scalar); `readonly JsonScalar[]` parameter composes with zod's contravariant `refine` parameter on any scalar-item array without a cast.

**packages/spec/src/marketplace/taxonomy.zod.ts — holds.**

- *Against the ruling it implements (seat ruling A, 20:12Z/20:14Z)*: exactly the three lines the ruling allowed — the import, the predicate swap to the declared constant with the same expression, and the type-only bound — and no other token in the file moves. The message, the `min`/`max` and the `describe` on both callers are untouched, and the ADR-side meaning ("a facet value counts once") is now a published keyword rather than a dropped refinement.
- *Against its first consumers* (`package.zod.ts`, `marketplace.zod.ts`, `template-manifest.zod.ts`): every one passes the facet schema by reference with at most `.optional()` around it; the bound is satisfied by both `z.enum` items; no consumer composes `distinct()` directly (it is not exported). The accept set each consumer sees is unchanged (①.1).
- *Trying to break it*: the bound `z.ZodType<JsonScalar>` could be made tighter as `z.ZodType<JsonScalar, JsonScalar>` to refuse coercing items at compile time, but that would not catch `.trim()`/`.toLowerCase()` (input and output both `string`), so it is not a substitute for the docblock note in the should-fix above; left as a remark, not a finding.

**Gates on the head** (conclusions are the verdicts): green — `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Type Check · source gates`, every `Lint ·` family, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build UI Deps`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Auto Label`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `filter`. Still running at the time this record was rendered and read as pending, not green: `Build Core` (the ledger gate in `build-schemas.ts` and the generated artifacts), `Type Check · workspace` (the `z.ZodType<JsonScalar>` bound's own program), `Test Core` 1/8-8/8 (the new pins and `dropped-refinements.test.ts`), `Type Check UI`. Also green since: `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`. No red check-run on the head at render time; the pending four are the gate verdicts for ①.2, ①.6 and the test pins, and the record is to be re-read against them before enqueue.

**Findings**
- must-fix (②): the changeset and PR body declare `Clause-②: no` with no arm for a diff that narrows a published accept set at 14 sites; they owe `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the `**BREAKING (published artifact narrows)**` banner and the single `<!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) … -->` marker in the changeset body, the `Skills-docs:` line in the PR body, and the dogfood battery pinned on the resulting head. Level stays `patch`.
- should-fix (④, refinement-projection.ts): the `unique-items` exactness argument and `UNIQUE_SCALAR_ITEMS`'s docblock must state that the item schema's parse has to be the identity on scalars (no coercion, trim, case-fold or transform), or a future composer publishes a file that reads `projected` while wider than the runtime.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dd7ed18f7456bbcb3b08139245e919ad6bc7875f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/marketplace/taxonomy.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/refinement-projection.ts + .changeset/31036-unique-items-projection.md and the PR body (read for ②), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/review-checklist.md (the readers the ② fix is judged against). Delta review by the same reviewer of the FAIL record 6695604767 on `da4e41dd`: the delta `da4e41dd..dd7ed18f` is one commit touching two files (the changeset, +5/−1; `src/shared/refinement-projection.ts`, +21 docblock lines); every other file of the PR is byte-identical to the reviewed head, so ①.1-①.8 and ④'s taxonomy.zod.ts judgment of the prior record carry over unchanged. Inputs: the delta diff, PR #31047 body and title on this head, the dev's round-2 report (comment 6696583372 on #31036), the check-runs on `dd7ed18f` (one read: 57 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure, 0 in progress). Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept sets unchanged by the delta (right).** The delta moves no code: the only `src` change is comment text inside two docblocks in `refinement-projection.ts`; no token outside a `/** … */` block moves, so the runtime accept set, the 14 projected sites, the ledger rows and the public surface are exactly those judged on `da4e41dd` (prior record ①.1-①.8), and the gate verdicts for them are now in: `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Test Core` 1-8 and `Type Check UI` — pending at the prior render — all concluded `success` on this head.
2. **The published-artifact narrowing is now declared (right).** The changeset reads `Clause-②: no (narrowing) — …`; the arm is the first token of the parenthetical opened immediately after the value, which is exactly the shape `clause2-line.mjs:265-272` reads, and the em-dash reasoning after the closing paren is "trailing reasoning" the reader keeps and does not grade. `Check Changeset` is green on the head, and the dev's local `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` read the file as `[BREAKING+clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — the two breaking signals (arm, banner) and the disposition, which is the reading the prior record asked for.
